This is a WRITE task based on a real visual bug report from the site owner, who flagged a screenshot of the invoices/billing table's "Paid" status badge as "not good" — a plain green pill with white "Paid" text, which reads as generic/default-styled rather than matching the rest of the Nexion design language (other status badges/tags elsewhere in the app use a more considered style — pill shape, tone-appropriate glow/border, consistent sizing).

1. Find the invoices/billing table rendering this badge — likely `components/nx/BillingView.tsx` or an invoices-specific component (search for "Paid" status rendering, or a status-badge helper function/component used for invoice rows).
2. Compare its styling against how OTHER status badges/tags in the Nexion design system are built elsewhere in the app — search `app/globals.css` for the shared tag/badge classes (e.g. `.nx-tag`, `.badge`, or similar — this session's own audits found classes like `.badge`/`.badge-cyan`/`.badge-amber` used for tone-based badges elsewhere, e.g. in the What's New feature) and use the SAME established pattern/class for this "Paid" status instead of a one-off inline green pill, so it's visually consistent with the rest of the site rather than looking like a default/unstyled element.
3. While you're in this file, also double-check the currency symbol rendering in the same table — the screenshot shows amounts like "฿6,000" and "฿1,078.80" which look like they might be rendering the WRONG currency symbol (Thai Baht ฿ instead of USD $, or possibly this platform's real multi-currency display feature is picking the wrong currency for this user). Search for `CurrencyProvider`/`resolveDisplayCurrency` (mentioned in this codebase) and the actual formatting function used for these invoice amounts — confirm whether this is a real currency-detection bug (wrong currency being resolved/displayed) or just an oddly-rendered $ glyph in a particular font/weight that only LOOKS like ฿ in a screenshot. Report clearly which it is; only fix it if it's a genuine code bug (e.g. a wrong default currency, a locale-detection issue) — don't guess-fix formatting that might just be a screenshot rendering artifact.

Run `cd /opt/nxeon-v2 && npx tsc --noEmit` after any fix and resolve type errors. Do not commit — leave changes unstaged. Report back with file:line and a clear answer on the currency-symbol question.

content.content: # Nxeon v2 — the "Nexion" design fork **This is not the production tree.** It is a full fork of the Nxeon platform with a from-scratch visual language called **Nexion** built over the real backend. The code is real, the database is real, the money paths are real code — but `NXEON_SANDBOX=1`, so no VM is ever provisioned and no card is ever charged. Read `docs/NEXION-V2.md` next. This file is the operating manual; that one is the direction and the history of what has been built. --- ## Where you are, and what that changes This tree runs on **node-2** (`nxeon-fsn1`, `178.63.94.114`), and the work is meant to happen there. Check which box you are on before anything else: ```bash hostname # nxeon-fsn1 = node-2. Anything else = the primary node. ``` **On node-2 (`nxeon-fsn1`) — the normal case.** Edit here and build here: ```bash npx tsc --noEmit # always, before a build ./rebuild.sh # stop, build, restart. ~125s. ``` **On the PRIMARY node.** Do not build. The primary is an 8-core box that also runs the customer game-server VMs (darkeden-guard-sg, projectzomboid, dst, terraria, valheim…) and sits at load ~11 before anyone types anything. A `next build` there competes with paying customers for CPU. Edit if you must, then: ```bash scripts/deploy-node2.sh # ships the commit, typechecks + builds ON node-2 ``` It refuses to run on a dirty tree (it ships commits, not a working directory) and refuses to reset over commits node-2 has and the primary doesn't. **One source of truth at a time.** The deploy script does `git reset --hard` on node-2. Once you are working on node-2, the primary's copy is stale — do not deploy from it again without reconciling, or you will silently discard node-2's commits. The script checks for this and stops; take the stop seriously. ## The tree | | | |---|---| | Path | `/opt/nxeon-v2` | | Branch | `design/v2` | | Service | `nxeon-v2-web` on port **3021** | | Public URL | https://v2.q4w8zt3ky6vn2sm.nxeon.cloud | | Database | `nxeon_v2` on localhost — **separate** from prod and from the primary's own copy | | Logins | `/root/nxeon-v2-credentials.txt` (admin + a design customer account) | | Build log | `/tmp/nxeon-v2-build.log` | `rebuild.sh` skips the marketing site by default (~137 of ~195 route files, and it dominates a build we run by hand after every change). `NX_FULL=1 ./rebuild.sh` builds everything — do that before any staging or prod pass. Schema changes: `npm run db:push`. There are no migration files. The primary node and node-2 have **separate** `nxeon_v2` databases, so a push on one does nothing to the other. ## Reaching node-1 (live production) from here node-2 has **root SSH to node-1**, granted by the owner on 2026-09-11, because three things a Nexion session needs live only there: the board concept attachments (~500 MB across ~99 cards — the design source of truth), the production database (for checking a claim against real data instead of sandbox seed data), and the real production tree to compare the fork against. Use `scripts/node1.sh` rather than raw ssh — quoting a psql call through two levels of ssh is where this reliably goes wrong: ```bash scripts/node1.sh cards "dashboard" # find concept cards by title scripts/node1.sh board # list that card's attachments scripts/node1.sh pull # copy them to /tmp/board/ scripts/node1.sh db "select …" # query against PROD scripts/node1.sh sh '' # anything else ``` **That grant is wide, and node-1 runs every customer VM, the production database and the mail server — mistakes here are not sandboxed.** The `db` subcommand refusing obvious writes is a guard against a slip, not a security boundary; the access itself is full root. **Update, 2026-09-12: the owner authorized this session to build, deploy, and promote the Nexion portal to production directly from here** — including running `scripts/deploy-staging.sh` and `scripts/promote-production.sh` on node-1, and writing to the prod DB as those scripts require (`prisma db push --accept-data-loss` on the way to production is the expected, sanctioned behavior of that script, not a mistake to avoid). This supersedes the "treat it as read-only, ask first" rule that used to sit here — the routine build/deploy/promote path no longer needs a stop-and-ask. That authorization carries guardrails that are **not optional**: - **Take a fresh, named `pg_dump` snapshot immediately before any write to the prod DB**, the same discipline already used for the pre-merge backup (`pre--.dump` under `/root/db-backups` on node-1, pulled down to node-2 too). Never skip this because a daily timer already ran — the daily timer isn't synced to the moment you're about to change something. - **Stop and report before proceeding if a step turns out more destructive or irreversible than expected** — e.g. `prisma db push --accept-data-loss` reporting it would actually drop a column or table rather than just add one, a schema change that isn't purely additive, or anything that would disrupt a customer mid-session in a way the sanctioned scripts don't already account for. "Automatic" covers the routine, expected path; it does not mean an unexpected destructive step gets waved through. - **Anything outside the build/deploy/promote workflow is still stop-and-ask** — touching customer credentials, hand-editing `/opt/nxeon` outside the sanctioned scripts, restarting a service those scripts don't themselves restart, or touching any of the `/opt/nxeon-*` siblings that belong to other sessions. The authorization is for shipping this fork to production, not a blanket lift of every caution on this box. ## Rules that are not negotiable 1. **Never fabricate.** No invented stats, ratings, reviews, player counts, ETAs or capabilities. If a number cannot be read from the database or from a real upstream, the field stays empty and the UI says why. This tree has already had hash-derived star ratings and fake customer reviews removed once — do not reintroduce that shape. When a source cannot answer, say so; never render a `0` that reads as a real measurement. 2. **Never run a manual, ad hoc build in `/opt/nxeon`.** Clobbering its `.next` with a raw `npm run build` has taken the admin panel down before. Running the sanctioned `scripts/promote-production.sh` (see "Reaching node-1" above) is fine — it exists specifically to update production without that failure mode; improvising your own build command in that directory is not. 3. **Never `pkill -f` by pattern on either box.** `pkill -f "next start"` restarted live production once. Kill by port PID or systemd unit. 4. **Never `git add -A` in a symlinked worktree** — it can replace prod's real `node_modules` with a self-referential symlink. 5. **Ask before touching credentials** on live customer infrastructure, and before spending on any paid third-party tool. 6. **Never send a support-ticket reply** without explicit sign-off. 7. **`/opt/nxeon-sandbox` belongs to a different session.** Leave it alone. 8. Secrets are gitignored. Never commit `.env` or a credentials file. ## Verification discipline A change is not done until it is **deployed and screenshotted**. There is a login-and-capture script: ```bash node scripts/shot.mjs /tmp/out /dashboard/directory /dashboard/settings # defaults to the design customer account; override with NX_EMAIL / NX_PASS ``` Playwright scripts must live inside `/opt/nxeon-v2` so the module resolves. The tip must be a named ref: `A..design/v2`. - **A positioned `fixed; z-0` aurora layer paints above static content.** Page content needs `relative z-[1]`. - **A `backdrop-filter` ancestor becomes the containing block for `fixed` children** — `createPortal` to `document.body` instead. - **Never size a fixed overlay from a header's height.** That is the header's bottom edge only when nothing sits above it, and the sandbox banner does. Let the layout place things. - **`mask-composite` is unevenly supported** — nest two single-axis masks. - **An `` that fails before hydration never fires `onError`.** Check `el.complete && el.naturalWidth === 0` on mount. - **`fetch` cannot report request-body progress in any browser.** Upload progress needs `XMLHttpRequest.upload.onprogress`. - **Shell-level React providers are easy to drop.** The Nexion shell omitted `ComposeProvider`, then `TerminalDockProvider`, then `MatrixProvider` — each took a whole feature down invisibly, because the crash only appears on a route a smoke test does not walk. Anything added to `components/portal/Shell.tsx` must be added to `components/nx/Shell.tsx` too. ## Conventions inherited from the platform (still true here) - Every VM state change goes through a `Job` row. The web app never calls Proxmox mutation endpoints directly. - One in-flight job per server. - Wallet amounts are integer cents. - Admin-only actions call `requireAdmin()` and refuse to render while impersonating. - Charts are dependency-free SVG in `components/ui/charts.tsx`. Do not add a charting library. ## Inherited instructions that do NOT apply here The production `CLAUDE.md` this replaced is kept at `docs/CLAUDE-production-inherited.md` for reference. It describes the PRIMARY node. To avoid a very expensive mistake: - **Do not** run `systemctl restart nxeon-web nxeon-worker` — that is production. This tree's unit is `nxeon-v2-web`. - **Do not** publish docs to `revsports.ca/docs` from here. - ~~Do not run `scripts/promote-production.sh` or `scripts/deploy-staging.sh`~~ — **superseded 2026-09-12.** The owner authorized running these directly from this session; see the guardrails in "Reaching node-1" above. - There is no post-commit auto-push hook on node-2, and there should not be: `design/v2` is a design fork, not something to push to `origin` casually.
